coverage.limitations: This baseline does not claim to reconstruct messages that are not present in the repository or visible context.

requirements.statement: An earlier plan proposed automatically installing Ollama and pulling qwen3:4b as part of first-run setup.
acceptance: Historical intent remains visible for migration review

requirements.statement: Sumika must be usable as a daily desktop Agent while retaining the first-version character, Avatar, desktop-pet, and local-data experience.
acceptance: A documented entry point starts the product
A real repository task can be completed with a recoverable result

requirements.statement: Windows is the stable desktop target; macOS and Linux expose direct Core startup first, with native Tauri launchers explicitly experimental or reserved.
acceptance: Platform-specific startup documentation is separate
Launchers do not install or update dependencies automatically

requirements.statement: Fixed navigation and status regions remain stable while the right content area scrolls independently and exposes accessible error states.
acceptance: Navigation does not move when content grows
Status items have keyboard focus and no misleading success state

requirements.statement: Chat keeps the latest record visible, reports sending/failure/cancelled/unconfigured states, and never emits a Fake reply.
acceptance: A new message scrolls to the latest record
Unavailable providers produce an actionable error

requirements.statement: Each character has an independent display name; Sumika is the project name, not a forced character name.
acceptance: Two characters can be displayed with different names
Renaming does not change project identity

requirements.statement: Structured persona fields enter the Provider system message in a fixed order, while the first greeting remains temporary context.
acceptance: Provider fixtures receive the system message
The greeting is not persisted as a chat message

requirements.statement: VRM Avatars render centered, face the user, support natural pose, idle motion, and bounded cursor following, and degrade safely when optional rig features are absent.
acceptance: VRM 0 orientation is corrected
Missing humanoid/lookAt features do not crash the viewer

requirements.statement: Desktop-pet mode is visually transparent, shows only Avatar plus a compact chat bar, and supports native window dragging without dragging controls.
acceptance: The overlay background is transparent
Model drag and chat input remain independently usable

requirements.statement: Provider connections are reusable profiles with tested endpoints, editable templates, draft/archive states, and explicit enablement.
acceptance: A profile can be saved and tested without exposing its secret
A draft cannot be silently enabled

requirements.statement: Ollama and model installation are user choices; qwen3:4b is an optional template, not a mandatory startup default.
acceptance: Startup works without Ollama
No provider is silently created or enabled for a new user

requirements.statement: Provider and ZCode credentials remain in protected storage or the provider's supported login session and never enter project data, logs, or model context.
acceptance: Secret values are absent from SQLite and logs
ZCode adapter never reads token files

requirements.statement: CC Switch import is versioned and previewed, stores endpoints, redacts secrets, and never executes imported JavaScript or unknown protocol versions.
acceptance: Known v1 fixtures import after confirmation
Unknown versions and executable scripts fail closed

requirements.statement: Unavailable providers, models, credentials, and runtimes fail explicitly and never fall back to Fake or silently paid routes.
acceptance: Health failure is visible as not ready
A failed free route requires an explicit alternative

requirements.statement: DSH is the default Harness adapter, while Core, UI, Tauri, Avatar, Browser, and Workspace remain runtime-neutral capability boundaries.
acceptance: A minimal non-DSH runtime can satisfy the stable contract
Unsupported capabilities fail explicitly

requirements.statement: The Agent surface exposes real Session, Plan, Execute, events, tools, approvals, MCP, Skills, Subagents, and failure recovery where the selected runtime supports them.
acceptance: Unsupported runtime capabilities are not rendered as working controls
Fixed DSH composition passes isolated protocol smoke

requirements.statement: MCP connections enter DSH through a previewed and approved user Preset with mount validation, protected credentials, and fail-closed handling for unknown or executable fields.
acceptance: A stdio or HTTP configuration can be reviewed before it is mounted
Unknown fields and unverified servers cannot execute

requirements.statement: Skills have an auditable discover, load, approve, revoke, and invoke lifecycle bound to an isolated Profile and the current Agent Session.
acceptance: Unverified source or permissions keep a Skill disabled
A Skill can be revoked without leaving an active registration

requirements.statement: DSH Session and turn state remain the activity source of truth while Sumika Tasks provide a bounded projection with traceable checkpoint links.
acceptance: Task views reflect session, approval, failure, cancellation, and retry events
The projection does not create a second active turn state

requirements.statement: Repository edits happen in a checked Workspace with checkpoints, file-level diff, exact restore, worktree support, and previewed local commit.
acceptance: Execute and Plan Review approval checkpoint before writes
Restore and commit require exact confirmation

requirements.statement: Same-type plugins are replaceable; community plugins require isolated license, API, permission, uninstall, and end-to-end validation before approval.
acceptance: A rejected plugin remains disabled
A validated plugin can be approved without coupling Core to its internals

requirements.statement: A read-only unified catalog exposes real implementations for each capability across local and cloud providers, external software, Harnesses, plugins, Skills, MCP, and isolated browser sessions without becoming a second routing or configuration source.
acceptance: Entries are grouped by capability and expose bounded source, transport, processing location, status, permissions, and selected/selectable metadata
A source failure leaves other groups available and reports only a stable error class
Fake/Stub/Placeholder entries and credential/path-like values are absent from RPC, HTTP, and UI projections
Web-chat candidates are marked as manual login and are never presented as API Providers

requirements.statement: Desktop software must be replaceable capability implementations behind a stable DesktopAdapter boundary for app protocols, Electron CDP, Windows UI Automation, and explicitly approved foreground takeover.
acceptance: A transport client can be registered through a generic adapter without changing Core or UI policy
An unavailable or unimplemented transport returns an explicit unavailable result and never fabricates window actions

requirements.statement: Desktop automation must use explicit registration, single-writer profile leases, approval-bound control, and bounded redacted audit metadata without exposing credentials, window contents, paths, or global input.
acceptance: Lease conflicts, approval-token reuse, nested credential input, and uncertain sends are covered by repeatable tests
Core shutdown releases only sessions created by that instance and does not terminate unrelated applications

requirements.statement: BrowserSkill handles browser mechanics while Sumika enforces isolated profiles, sensitive-action approval, human handoff, and download quarantine.
acceptance: Credential and CAPTCHA actions pause for the user
Downloads remain quarantined until confirmation

requirements.statement: Existing data and archives are preserved; destructive deletion, force overwrite, global runtime changes, and unapproved external writes are prohibited.
acceptance: Recovery path exists for cleanup and restore
Secrets and user data do not enter the repository

requirements.statement: A one-click entry only checks and starts installed, version-managed Core, Harness, and desktop services, then releases processes and ports created by that instance on exit.
acceptance: An unavailable dependency produces an actionable status instead of an implicit install
Closing Sumika does not terminate an unrelated external service

requirements.statement: Agent observability is bounded, redacted, aggregatable, and suitable for comparing models and plugins without storing content.
acceptance: Daily reports include latency and outcome aggregates
Prompts, outputs, tool payloads, files, and credentials are absent

requirements.statement: External projects, plugins, memory systems, and quota sources are versioned in a knowledge registry; discovery and evaluation do not auto-enable changes.
acceptance: Each entry has version, license, capability, check time, and conclusion
Install/upgrade/enable remains approval-gated

requirements.statement: External code, models, animation, icons, and behavioral references must have auditable source, version, license, and usage records.
acceptance: A source ledger entry exists before packaging or copying external material
Unverified assets remain reference-only

requirements.statement: Use ZCode's time-limited entitlement and Zhipu's authorized free quota before consuming expensive model capacity when quality and safety gates allow.
acceptance: Eligible free routes appear as candidates only after health/auth checks
Unknown quota is not labeled free

requirements.statement: Keep ZCode, Zhipu, and Ollama in an extensible model catalog, with ZCode represented as a Harness adapter and Zhipu/Ollama as provider profiles.
acceptance: Harness and Provider identity are not conflated
A future Harness can reuse catalog and policy types

requirements.statement: ZCode integration uses its supported app-server session protocol and login state, never token extraction or an unverified endpoint.
acceptance: Handshake and session operations are isolated and auditable
Missing login state fails closed

requirements.statement: Zhipu quota claims are dynamic and may be marked free only from an official usage source or explicit user confirmation.
acceptance: Credential Manager is the only secret store
Expired or unauthenticated quota is not selected

requirements.statement: Choose models by task difficulty and risk after satisfying a minimum quality/capability gate, then optimize for free quota, cost, and latency.
acceptance: Routing decisions include difficulty, quality gate, cost, and reason codes
A low-quality candidate is not selected only because it is cheap

requirements.statement: The router must not silently escalate from a free route to a paid route when quota is exhausted or health changes.
acceptance: The user receives an explicit alternative or pause
Automatic mode remains bounded by a hard budget

requirements.statement: Default routing is recommendation-then-confirmation; users may opt into fully automatic selection per preset or session.
acceptance: A recommendation explains candidates and impact
Full-auto cannot bypass security, quality, or budget gates

requirements.statement: Ollama remains available for no-quota local health and protocol tests, with the smaller model for fast smoke and the 4B model for fuller local validation.
acceptance: Model listing health check does not generate content
Local smoke never stops or rewrites the user's existing service

requirements.statement: Quota checks run only after a configurable interval and when the system is idle; login, OTP, CAPTCHA, payment, and entitlement claims require the user.
acceptance: Startup does not poll repeatedly during active work
Protected actions pause with a clear handoff

requirements.statement: Model and plugin comparisons use fixed task cohorts and bounded observability rather than latency alone, and cannot auto-change production policy from weak samples.
acceptance: Reports include sample/version comparability
Prompts and outputs are absent from evaluation records

requirements.statement: Future multi-character scenes keep persona, session, memory namespace, model policy, and budget independent while separating temporary interaction context from world location.
acceptance: A future design can represent multiple participants without sharing memory implicitly
No current single-character data is rewritten

requirements.statement: Memory is an optional, replaceable Provider capability scoped to a character or Agent, and different implementations can be selected and compared without implicit sharing.
acceptance: A memory implementation can be replaced without rewriting character data
Shared memory is never enabled without an explicit scope and policy

requirements.statement: Audio, vision, Live2D, external animation libraries, VirtualWorld, LifeAgent, RemoteRunner, Android, and formal multi-platform packaging remain deferred until real modules and safety boundaries exist.
acceptance: Deferred capabilities are not presented as production-ready
Adding one later requires a real adapter and license/security review
